question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. If $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(A))=2.$

II. If $B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(B))=3.$

III. If $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(C))=2.$

II. If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14129912/assets/b6faca669e9264d1e796de5798ac786a3b82ac3316f528c6e0a0b35eab0ed38f.svg) then $\textrm{dim(Null}(B))=0$

III. If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14129912/assets/c75af18d61b1c04c404e5a5a1ffaf86a99f5a1aa911bfac537ae866b2404d231.svg) then $\textrm{dim(Null}(C))=1$
current_example.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- Statement I is false. The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd column). So, 

$$
\textrm{dim(Null}(A))=1.
$$

- Statement II is false. The matrix $B$ has $1$ pivot column and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and $3$rd columns). So, 

$$
\textrm{dim(Null}(B))=2.
$$

- Statement III is true. The matrix $C$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$nd column). So, 

$$
\textrm{dim(Null}(C))=1.
$$

Therefore, only statement III is true.
